analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It adds one table row, at head line 2206, documenting the watchdog crash-restart timing: the next check after an outage is seen (1-2 min), with a 300 s grace period when the restart would continue a crash-loop chain. No code, config, authorization, attestation, encryption or wire behavior changes. The row cites WatchdogDecision.swift and WatchdogPolicy.graceSeconds, which were not supplied, so I could not verify the numbers against source.

I read the supplied base excerpts (lines 802-1729, which cover Autopilot, add-on hold, sandbox setup, stop/restart, status, doctor and update) and found no change in them. The changed row sits outside those excerpts, so the head side of the surrounding table was not examined in full.

Relevant threat model entries are T-043 (the watchdog and its rollback authority run in the same replaceable provider binary) and T-046/T-047 (availability and lifecycle). The row is availability and lifecycle documentation only and does not weaken a mitigation. It could slightly affect operator expectations about crash-loop recovery timing. If the stated values drift from WatchdogDecision.swift, the documentation would be inaccurate, but that is not a security regression.

No findings. Remaining question: the documented timing values were not checked against the Swift source, which was outside the supplied evidence and is not material to security.
